commitResults.messageTitle: Changed chatbot name to Gatsby, added greeting, joke and farewell messages

commitResults.messageBody:
Added Echo functionality to the Gatsby chatbot.

The Gatsby chatbot will now take in string inputs from the user and echo it back, only terminating upon a "bye" or "bye bye" prompt (non case-sensitive).
Edge cases detection is also added to identify terminating prompts, whereby any arbitrary number of spaces between "bye bye" will be correctly identified.

Limitations:
* Intra-word spacing is not detected as a terminating prompt yet (e.g "bye by e").

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the ability to store whatever text the user enters and display it back when requested.
commitResults.messageBody:
Able to store up to 100 messages entered by the user.
Chatbot now no longer just echoes what is entered by the user.
Key in "list" to display the full list of texts entered by the user.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the ability to mark tasks as done. Optionally, add the ability to change the status back to not done.
commitResults.messageBody: Implemented new Task class to be used in the list as well.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UI testing workflow for code changes
Add support for tracking three types of tasks:
commitResults.messageBody:
ToDos: tasks without any date/time attached to them,
 - todo visit new theme park
Deadlines: tasks that need to be done before a specific date/time,
 - deadline submit report /by 11 Oct 2026 5pm
Events: tasks that start at a specific date/time and end at a specific date/time,
 - (a) event team project meeting /from 2 Oct 2026 2pm /to 4pm
 - (b) orientation week /from 10 Oct 2026 /to 11 Oct 2026

commitResults.messageTitle: Teach the chatbot to deal with errors such as incorrect inputs entered by the user.

Add support for deleting tasks from the list. Use Java Collections classes for storing data. ArrayList was chosen because it offers many advantages (e.g., dynamic sizing, easy to find/add/delete items) over using a primitive data structure such as a normal array.
Use Java enums, if applicable (i.e., if enums a natural fit for somewhere in the current code).
Save the tasks on the hard disk automatically whenever the task list changes and load the data from the hard disk when the chatbot starts up.
Add functionality for chatbot to recognise date and time formats for event and deadline for it to store in the local file.

commitResults.messageBody: Move Gatsby's in-memory task collection and its basic add, lookup, remove, size, and empty checks into a dedicated TaskList class. Keep persistence behind a read-only view so Storage continues to save the same task data without changing console behavior.

Move Gatsby's banner, welcome message, scanner lifecycle, separators, and console output behind a Ui class. Keep command handling and all user-facing text unchanged so the refactoring improves separation of concerns without altering behavior.

Move command recognition, alias handling, whitespace normalization, and payload extraction out of Gatsby and Command.fromInput into a dedicated Parser. Keep Command as the command vocabulary and preserve all existing input behavior.

Separate parsed command vocabulary into CommandType so Command can represent executable actions. Add the abstract Command protocol with execute and isExit, then move goodbye behavior into ExitCommand. Keep the remaining task operations in Gatsby for this incremental stretch step and preserve the existing UI behavior.

Move task-list rendering, including the empty-list message and numbered task output, into a concrete ListCommand implementation. Keep Gatsby responsible only for selecting and executing the command so the existing console behavior remains unchanged.

Move todo, deadline, and event creation out of Gatsby into dedicated Command subclasses. Centralize shared payload validation, keyword splitting, task persistence, and creation feedback in the command base class while preserving all existing date parsing and user-facing messages. Keep Gatsby responsible for selecting the command object and executing it.

Move mark, unmark, and delete behavior out of Gatsby into dedicated Command subclasses. Centralize task-number validation, completion-state updates, persistence, and task-count reporting in the command layer while preserving all existing success and error messages.

Provide project-specific guidance based on the SE-EDUCATION Java standard.

Apply the conventions consistently to production and test code so future
changes use the same naming, layout, import, and documentation rules.

Provide project-specific guidance based on the SE-EDUCATION Git conventions.

Use the guidance for commit subjects, explanatory bodies, and meaningful
kebab-case branch names throughout the project.

Require the project-specific Java and Git skills for future work.

Keep code changes aligned with the SE-EDUCATION Java conventions and require
commit and branch work to follow the corresponding Git conventions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Model classes: Apply Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
The core task model classes use inconsistent braces, mutable fields that never
change, and incomplete API documentation.

Apply the project Java conventions, document the public model API, and use
clear final fields while preserving task display and save-file formats.

commitResults.messageBody:
Configure Checkstyle with the SE-EDUCATION coding standard and add
test-file suppressions. Fix existing import-order and formatting
violations without changing application behaviour.

Add a JavaFX chat window that reuses Gatsby's existing command-processing
and persistence logic.

- Support command entry through Enter and Send.
- Add Gatsby and user avatars, including the starting joke.
- Close the application for all supported exit aliases.
- Preserve existing console behavior with regression coverage.

Allow users to view Gatsby's command reference using `help` or `?`.
Add unit and UI coverage, and fix UI constructor ordering for Checkstyle.
